question: The AI's order command and its validity.

slots_noted.0x1E2A90: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder(CEU3AI* ai, SaveToken orderType, CUnit* unit, int provinceId, void* provinceIds, int* from, int* to, void* x)
addresses.comment: The real order factory behind 0x89ABD0. When orderType is 0x3A5 (`invasion`) it first walks ai->+0x40 (the unit agents) setting each agent's +0x86 = 1, then refuses outright when unit->+0x158 (falling back) is non-zero, and otherwise allocates a 0xA0-byte **CSetOrderCommand** (its constructor 0x1E1E70, vftable 0x11C901C by RTTI), copies the province list into it (+0x84..+0x8C) and posts it - so the AI's order is asked nothing of the click's tests, only CSetOrderCommand::IsValid (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 122). CAIInvasion stage 2 calls it directly at 0x8A0977 with the eight arguments, passing the now/sunrise pair as `from`/`to`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x49AD00-0x49AE12 read live 2026-11-18; the RTTI of the table the constructor writes.
addresses.revises: comment - the object is a CSetOrderCommand, and it is posted

addresses.name: CSetOrderCommand::CSetOrderCommand
addresses.no_signature: stack arguments past the object (+8) not followed; ret 0x18
addresses.comment: **CSetOrderCommand's constructor**, the object on the stack (+8), `ret 0x18`. Writes the CCommand base vftable 0x11B4F74 and type id 0x18D, then its own vftable **0x11C901C** at 0x1E1EEC - RTTI `.?AVCSetOrderCommand@@`; slot 6 is its execute (0x1E1F90) and slot 14 CSetOrderCommand::IsValid (0x1E2A90). Called by CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder (0x49AD00). The name is from the RTTI. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 122.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x1E1E70-0x1E1F80 and the RTTI of 0x11C901C read live 2026-11-18.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder(CEU3AI* ai, SaveToken orderType, CUnit* unit, int provinceId@EDI)
addresses.comment: ret 0xC with a fourth argument in EDI, which is consistent at all five call sites in CAIInvasion stage 3 (0x8A0A2D, 0x8A0B22, 0x8A102F, 0x8A118B and the 0x8A1122 arm): EDI is loaded with a province id in the instruction before the pushes. It builds a one-element province list and tail-calls 0x89AD00 at 0x89ACD0. The order types seen through it are the save tokens 0x18D `none`, 0x3A8 `transport` and 0x3A5 `invasion`. CAIUnit_CheckLandMarches's strategic redeployment goes this way too, and an enemy's province at its end is no refusal: three to the rebels' 6151 seen accepted in July 1941 (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 122).
addresses.revises: comment - the march check's redeployment, seen

addresses.name: CSetOrderCommand::IsValid
addresses.comment: **CSetOrderCommand slot 14**, 0x1E2A90 to the `ret` at 0x1E2B2D: what its execute (slot 6, 0x1E1F90) asks first. The unit's id pair (+0x40/+0x44) resolved and kept at +0x3C - none: false; the province (+0x68) nought: false; a unit whose slot 17 or slot 16 answers true (a fleet or a wing) must have a base (+0x98). **No range** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 84): an order the AI issues through CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder goes beyond a fleet's range from base. The name is ours. **No test of an enemy either**: the AI's strategic redeployment to a province the rebels hold is valid, three seen accepted in July 1941 (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 122).
addresses.evidence: Recording wr15, tick 60807913: three strategic_redeployment orders to 6151 (REB) in the save.
